text:
lina: noticing 95th latency jitter on host-rack-9 (apac-sg1) for fractional-dedicated slices. spike aligns with tenant Z bursts around 03:00 UTC.

rohan: saw it on the nightly sweep. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress?var-host=host-rack-9&from=now-3h

diego: paste quick ifconfig/ethtool and IRQ stats? want to rule out TOR flap vs NIC scheduling.

lina: ifconfig snapshot:
```
eth0: flags=4163 mtu 1500
    tx packets 3.1M  bytes 42GB (42.0 GB)
    RX errors 0  dropped 0  overruns 0  frame 0
eth1: flags=4163 mtu 1500
    tx packets 210k  bytes 2.6GB
    RX errors 25  dropped 6  overruns 0  frame 0
```

lina: ethtool -S eth1 shows VF queue drops for vf2 during bursts.

rohan: risky: this host was marked "high-vf-density" after we consolidated to save slots. Noisy tenant Z probably saturating MSI-X vectors and causing soft-irqs to pile up.

kait: infra-bot: open a quick mitigation ticket and suggest ephemeral VLAN carveout? moving tenant Z to spare-dedicated-eq pool would preserve SLO but costs more.

infra-bot: [NOTICE] created ticket INFRA-5129 (P2) for host-rack-9 egress jitter. Notified oncall. :bell:

rohan: prefer ephemeral steer for 20m -> spare-dedicated-eq-apac to stop neighbor bleed while we capture traces. Anyone object?

diego: +1. also capture /proc/interrupts and /var/log/kern.log at 1s resolution for 5m. suspect irq affinity misbalance.

lina: running commands now:
```
./bin/routectl steer --tenant Z --target spare-dedicated-eq-apac --ttl 1200 --reason "noisy-vf jitter"
cat /proc/interrupts > /tmp/irqs_before.txt
journalctl -k -o short-iso --since "5 minutes ago" > /tmp/kern_tail.txt
tcpdump -w /tmp/host-rack-9-egress.pcap -i eth1 -s 0 -c 20000
```

kait: tagging @platform-costs: spare-dedicated-eq billing ~2.5x for the next 20m. estimate incremental cost for this window ~+$0.6. Fine?

harsha: ops note: if this repeats nightly, we should add a scheduler-preference rule that avoids packing VF-heavy tenants on the same NIC. CAPEX vs OPEX tradeoff.

rohan: one-off throttle as experiment: Diego, can you try a per-vf shaping rule to cap tenant Z to 500mbit and see if latency stabilizes?

diego: will run this in lab first, but quick snippet that might work on host:
```
# on vf2 interface
tc qdisc add dev vf2 root tbf rate 500mbit burst 32k latency 50ms
```

lina: steer applied. infra-bot audit: 

infra-bot: [AUDIT] steer invoked by lina: tenant Z -> spare-dedicated-eq-apac TTL=1200

rohan: after steer, tail latency on vf1 consumers dropped ~40% in last 2mins. eth1 RX errors still present but no cross-slice spike. Looks like isolation helped.

kait: please attach pcap and irq dump to INFRA-5129. Also add runbook step: "if VF driver shows repeated rx_errors > 10 within 5m, consider immediate steer + per-vf throttle."

harsha: for long-term: propose experiment matrix: 1) VF throttle thresholds, 2) scheduler soft-label vf-sensitive hosts, 3) measure OPEX delta for keeping spare-dedicated pools. I'll put together numbers.

diego: one more note: vendor driver 1.2.3 had known flow-steer regressions under bursty TX. we'll repro in bench and test 1.2.4.

lina: thanks team. I'll leave steer for 20m and monitor. infra-bot will auto-revert if stable after TTL. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
